target.description: With allowed_domains enabled, BrowserContext._is_url_allowed compares netloc.lower().split(':')[0] with permitted domains. A URL with an allowed domain in colon-bearing userinfo can pass that check while its parsed hostname names a disallowed navigation destination. The canonical allegation is browser domain allowlist bypass; server-side metadata access is not required or established.

matching_rules: A finding must make a concrete security allegation explaining the attacker-controlled input or action, intended restriction, and mechanism by which that restriction fails under the frozen deployment assumptions.

The finding must be consistent with supplied deployment context; it need not repeat every configuration value. Conditional claims are acceptable only when the stated condition matches the frozen case. Unsupported assumptions and ambiguous claims are unresolved until reviewed, not automatic hits or false positives.
One accepted allegation can match at most one canonical target. Multiple regions, aliases, duplicate findings and repeated scans do not increase the target count.

Match reviewers are blinded to scanner identity where practical; record any residual identity cues. Freeze target definitions and accepted locations before scanning; use independent adjudication for disputes and disclose who reviewed them.
